# Process Model Discovery from an Event Log — Accumulated Guidance

## Directly-Follows Graph (DFG) Construction
- Compute the directly-follows graph by counting **ALL consecutive-pair occurrences across every case (raw frequency)**, not the number of distinct cases containing each pair. A pair that appears multiple times within one case should be counted multiple times. This is the standard directly-follows count used in process mining.
- **Do NOT use set-based (unique case) counting** to determine edge support — this underestimates support for edges that repeat within a case and leads to incorrect threshold decisions that miss frequently-traversed edges.

## Choosing a Support Cutoff
- To choose the support cutoff, look at the **raw frequency distribution** of all directly-follows pairs and select a threshold that keeps the pairs with meaningful occurrence counts.
- A threshold in the range of **9–20 occurrences** typically gives a good starting point on logs of a few hundred cases. Evidence shows that at threshold=9, the reference implementation achieves ~96% coverage, meaning nearly all important edges have frequency ≥ 9.
- **The threshold should be chosen to maximize the balanced score (coverage × selectivity)**. Thresholds above 9 (e.g., 10–15) can simultaneously improve selectivity and maintain or improve coverage if the dropped edges are true low-frequency deviations. **Explicitly test thresholds 10, 11, and 12 and compare balanced scores before settling** on a final value.
- To find the optimal threshold, compute **balanced_score = coverage × (1 − edges_kept / total_edges)** for each threshold from 9 to 20, and pick the one with the highest balanced score rather than relying solely on identifying a "natural gap" in the frequency distribution.

## Post-Filtering Validation
- **Do not apply any additional filtering or edge pruning beyond the raw frequency threshold.** Every edge whose raw frequency meets or exceeds the threshold must be included in the final model — do not drop edges based on secondary heuristics such as reachability, connectivity, or "coherence" of subprocesses. Missing even one high-traversal edge can disqualify many cases from coverage.
- **Do NOT discard edges because their source or target node appears unreachable from the start activity.** Reachability filtering and BFS-based pruning are a primary cause of missing high-frequency edges and large coverage gaps. Include all qualifying edges regardless of whether the resulting graph is fully connected.
- When verifying which edges meet the threshold, **explicitly list ALL edges** — not just those forming a "clean" connected subgraph — and confirm each one is included in the final model. If the resulting graph is disconnected or has nodes that seem unreachable from the start, include them anyway. The coverage metric rewards completeness over structural cleanliness.
- **Measure coverage** as the fraction of complete cases where every consecutive pair in the trace is present in the filtered edge set. Use this metric to validate the chosen threshold.

## Diagnosing Coverage Gaps
- When the coverage of the discovered model is significantly below the reference (e.g., >5 percentage points gap at the same threshold), the cause is likely **missing edges that meet the threshold**. Verify by listing every edge with frequency ≥ threshold and confirming all are included in the final model.
- **If your model has very few nodes (e.g., 8 out of 25 activities) at threshold=10, this is a strong signal that edges were silently excluded by reachability pruning or BFS filtering.** Re-run the threshold filter independently of any connectivity analysis to confirm the true edge count. The reference implementation at threshold=10 achieves ~96% coverage, implying it retains substantially more nodes and edges than 8 nodes / 17 edges.
- As a concrete diagnostic check: after choosing a threshold and collecting all qualifying edges, count the number of distinct nodes. **For a log with ~25 activities and ~400 cases, the node count should be approximately 12–15 or more.** Fewer than ~12 nodes at threshold=10 almost certainly indicates that valid edges have been dropped due to secondary filtering.
- Do **not** selectively include only edges that form "clean" subprocesses — include **all** edges above the threshold. Omitting even a small number of qualifying edges for aesthetic or structural reasons can cause a large drop in case coverage.
